purpose: Audit of the atmosphere model behind the reported peak density enhancement, answering twenty reviewer questions with computed values and testing four falsifiable explanations for the gap to He et al. 2023.

q01_exact_implementation.licence: no licence terms located for the compiled artefact; research-only pending verification (see third_party/licences/NRLMSISE-00-PROVENANCE.md)
q01_exact_implementation.implementation: The NRL Fortran NRLMSISE-00 source, compiled into the pymsis extension module msis00f and called through pymsis.msis.calculate(). No Python reimplementation of the model is used anywhere in this repository.

q02_model_version.meaning: 0 = NRLMSISE-00, the 2001 model; no licence terms located for the compiled artefact, research-only
q02_model_version.reason: NRLMSIS 2.0/2.1 is under a US Naval Research Laboratory academic-non-commercial licence and US Patent 10,641,925. A guard test parses the provider with ast and fails if any restricted version literal can reach msis.calculate.

q04_coefficient_files.note: NRLMSISE-00 carries its coefficients INSIDE the Fortran source, so there is no external coefficient file for version 0 to hash. The hashable artefact is the compiled extension module. The .parm files shipped alongside belong to NRLMSIS 2.0/2.1 and are NOT read by version 0; they are hashed here only to record that they were present and unused.

q05_model_switches.meaning: pymsis create_options index 8 is geomagnetic_activity: +1 selects daily-Ap mode, -1 selects storm-time mode in which the 7-element ap array is consumed. Every other switch is left at 1, its default, so no seasonal, diurnal, tidal or longitudinal term is suppressed.

q06_nrlmsise00_flags.no_note: NRLMSISE-00 does not produce NO; pymsis returns NaN in that column and the provider omits the key rather than writing a zero, because absence and zero are different claims.

q07_ap_mode.provider_rule: Nrlmsise00Provider._raw sets options=create_options(geomagnetic_activity=-1) and passes drivers.ap_history whenever that history is present; it falls back to [ap_daily] * 7 with options=None only when no history was supplied.

verification.method: The same drivers were run through both ap paths at the peak point. Identical results would prove the storm switch was not in force.

q08_solar_flux.rule: NRLMSISE-00 is fitted to the PREVIOUS day's observed F10.7; drivers_at applies that offset. The 81-day value is a centred mean of observed F10.7, never of adjusted F10.7.

q09_sampling.latitude_note: Held at 53.22 deg N, the orbital INCLINATION, for the whole series. It is not a latitude the vehicle occupied continuously: an inclined orbit reaches that latitude twice per revolution and spends most of its time below it.
q09_sampling.longitude_note: Held at 0 deg for the whole series, so mean local solar time equals UTC exactly and the diurnal cycle is aliased onto the storm time series rather than sampled across it.
q09_sampling.local_solar_time_coverage: All 24 hours, but only once each per day and perfectly correlated with UTC, so local time and storm phase cannot be separated in this series.

storm_reference.definition: Observed drivers at each instant: GFZ Kp/ap converted to the 7-element NRLMSISE-00 ap history, plus CelesTrak F10.7 (previous-day observed and 81-day centred average).

quiet_reference.definition: A COUNTERFACTUAL, not an observation: geomagnetic activity is set to ap = 4 (Kp ~ 1) in every element of the history while solar flux is held at the observed value, so the comparison isolates the geomagnetic storm from the solar-cycle background.
quiet_reference.source: counterfactual quiet baseline (ap=4.0) over observed solar flux

q12_density.definition: rho = sum over reported species of m_i * n_i. The species sum is used rather than the model's own total, so the density that drives drag is the same quantity the composition diagnostics describe.

q14_temperature.note: NRLMSISE-00 returns the kinetic temperature at the requested altitude. The exospheric temperature is available from pymsis but is not carried by this provider, so it is reported as absent rather than guessed.

q15_enhancement_calculation.what_varies_between_them: geomagnetic drivers only; solar flux held

comparisons.baseline_definition: Enhancement relative to a 10-DAY AVERAGED density from the same model at the same UT (Fang et al. section 4: 'The anomalies were calculated by subtracting the current values from the 10-day averaged densities from each model at the same UT'). This is neither this project's quiet-ap counterfactual nor He et al.'s reference days.
comparisons.averaging_domains: NOT AVERAGED. The 50-125 % span is the RANGE the simulated enhancement takes across locations and altitudes over the event. It is not a mean, not a profile, and it has no value at any single altitude.
comparisons.quoted_text: Based on WAM-IPE simulations, the neutral density enhancement for this event ranged from 50% to 125%, depending on location and altitude.
comparisons.note: CONTEXTUAL RANGE OVER A DOMAIN, NOT AN ALTITUDE PROFILE. The source gives the span as varying with location AND altitude, so no value for 210 km can be read out of it and none is produced. It is retained because it is the headline figure of the paper that studied this event, and it is what makes the model-family difference visible: the same paper reports NRLMSISE-00 at up to 20 % for the same event.
comparisons.summary: Fang et al. 2022 (WAM-IPE, 200-400 km domain), doi:10.1029/2022SW003193: NOT COMPARABLE with 17.1% - the source reports a range over 200-400 km that varies with location as well as height, so it states no value at 210 km and none can be read from it; the computed value is a 'point_peak' and this finding is a 'spatial_range'; the computed value is measured against a 'fixed_quiet_ap_counterfactual' and this finding against a 'n_day_model_mean'. q16_published_comparison.verdict:
Computed storm-time neutral mass density enhancement: 0.171 (17.1%), measured as a fraction of the quiet-time neutral mass density, at 210 km, defined as a 'point_peak' against a 'fixed_quiet_ap_counterfactual' baseline.
NO DIRECT COMPARISON IS AVAILABLE. None of the 8 published findings matches the computed value on all three of altitude, quantity definition and baseline: 7 fail on altitude, 8 on quantity definition and 8 on baseline. No agreement, disagreement, validation or bias classification is issued, and the per-finding positions below are context only. The previous claim that our fixed-point enhancement lay below all published modelled findings was unsupported. Corrected citations and altitude assignments place the result in its proper model-family context, but differences in sampling, averaging and baseline definitions prevent a direct numerical validation.
Provenance: 8 findings from 2 distinct papers (10.1029/2022SW003193, 10.1029/2023SW003521). Findings are not independent sources; several of these are reported by one paper.

nominal.refused: Fang et al. 2022 (WAM-IPE) supplies no altitude profile: its 50%-125% span is the range reported across 200-400 km AND across locations (Abstract (p. 1); Conclusions (p. 13)), so the source states no value at 210.0 km and this provider will not manufacture one. Use selection 'low' or 'high', which are the published extremes of the domain, and report them as a contextual range rather than as a value at this altitude.

refusal_outside_coverage.above the published altitude band: 505.0 km is outside the published altitude coverage of He et al. 2023 (MSIS2.0) (200-300 km). This provider does not extrapolate a published band beyond what its source supports.
refusal_outside_coverage.outside the published time window: 2022-02-08T00:00:00+00:00 is outside the published time coverage of He et al. 2023 (MSIS2.0) (2022-02-03T00:00:00+00:00 to 2022-02-05T00:00:00+00:00). This provider does not extrapolate a published band beyond what its source supports.

q17_published_envelope_comparison.reading: The envelope densities are the SAME quiet baseline scaled by the published enhancement. The ratio column is therefore the factor by which this project's storm density would have to rise to match each published source, at the same point, on the same baseline.

q18_observational_comparison.altitude_mismatch_warning: NEITHER measurement is at 210 km. Swarm-A flies at ~438 km and GRACE-FO at ~505 km, 228 km and 295 km ABOVE the Starlink staging altitude. Agreement or disagreement with them says nothing directly about the density at 210 km, because the storm-time enhancement varies with altitude. What the rows below DO establish is whether this model reproduces the observed enhancement at the altitudes where an observation exists at all.
q18_observational_comparison.no_observation_at_staging_altitude: There is no accelerometer-derived density at 210 km for this storm in the sources this project holds. The 210 km result is therefore unvalidated against observation and is reported as such.

q19_wind_sensitivity.justification: Magnitudes taken from the storm-wind scale this repository already cites: HWM14 storm-time winds at 210 km of several hundred m/s (providers.nrlmsise00.ZeroWindProvider), and the storm-time circulation simulated for this event by Fang et al. 2022, doi:10.1029/2022SW003193. Both signs are swept because the sign decides whether the wind adds to or subtracts from the relative speed.

geometry.along_track_projection_note: A zonal wind is not along-track. On a 53.22 degree orbit the eastward unit vector projects onto the along-track direction with a factor between cos(53.22 deg) = 0.598 at the equator and 1.0 at the orbit's highest latitude, so a wind of W m/s changes the relative speed by less than W. The deployment state is at the ascending node, i.e. the equator, which is the WEAKEST point of the orbit for a zonal wind; the orbit-mean column covers the rest.

q19_wind_sensitivity.lifetime_caveat: The lifetime column is a FIRST-ORDER estimate, not a propagated result. DragPropagator has no wind term, so a wind-resolved decay cannot be produced without changing the propagator. The estimate assumes lifetime scales as the reciprocal of the orbit-averaged rho * |v_rel|^2 at fixed density and fixed drag coefficient.

spread_against_published_msis_figures.synthesis: THERE IS NO GAP TO THE PUBLISHED MSIS FIGURE AT THIS ALTITUDE. The reported 17.1% at 210 km sits above He et al.'s 10%-15% for MSIS2.0 at 200 km, the nearest altitude they quote, and inside the 10%-25% their 200 and 300 km figures span. This section was built to explain a gap that existed only while a single 20-25% band was carried across the whole layer. What the section still measures is worth keeping: how wide the family of defensible values from this model is. This run's enhancement rises with altitude from 16.2% at 200 km to 27.9% at 300 km, so quoting it at 210 km and averaging it along a 210 x 338 km orbit differ mainly in how much of that altitude range they include. Maximising over place as well as time gives 21.1%. Replacing the counterfactual with a pre-storm OBSERVED baseline makes the enhancement SMALLER, not larger; the quiet-ap VALUE chosen inside that definition is a sensitive knob. The honest reading is that 17.1% is one defensible number from a family spanning roughly 16% to 28%, and that the family, not the single number, is what should be reported. THE REAL DISAGREEMENT IS WITH THE PHYSICS-BASED MODELS - WAM-IPE, CTIPe and MAGE run two to four times higher for this event - and both source papers report that difference themselves. It is a difference between model families, not evidence about the true atmosphere at 210 km.
spread_against_published_msis_figures.question: How wide is the family of defensible enhancement values this model produces for this event, and where do He et al. 2023's MSIS2.0 figures - about 10-15% at 200 km and 20-25% at 300 km - sit inside it? The earlier form of this question assumed a gap, by comparing a 210 km value against a band quoted at 300 km.

explanation_c_altitude_of_the_published_.hypothesis: He et al. quote 200 AND 300 km. The modelled enhancement rises with altitude, so a figure quoted at 300 km is not comparable to one computed at 210 km.
explanation_c_altitude_of_the_published_.reading: This run gives 16.2% at 200 km and 27.9% at 300 km. He et al.'s 10%-15% is a summary across those same two altitudes, and it lies OUTSIDE the range this run produces between them. A single number computed at 210 km is near the BOTTOM of that range by construction, because 210 km is near the bottom of the interval.

explanation_d_peak_definition.hypothesis: The reported peak is the maximum over TIME at one fixed place. The maximum over time AND place is larger.
